subject: Lokr, a self-hosted personal workspace for managing CVs, saved jobs, applications, and interview preparation.
scope: Extend the existing Lokr interface into twelve connected operational screens based on the supplied wireframe, while preserving the current dashboard, interaction model, responsive shell, and honest local-data boundaries.
primaryGoal: Help an individual job seeker move from saved job to reviewed CV, tracked application, and interview preparation through a coherent workspace.
audience: Individual job seekers using one self-hosted workspace.
offer: A private workspace that connects CV versions, jobs, applications, and interview preparation without overstating AI capabilities or backend persistence.
primaryAction: Add or save a job, then continue managing its application from the workspace.
creativeControl: Moderate. Retain the existing Lokr visual language and recompose the product workflows to follow the supplied wireframe. Use the wireframe as a layout and information-architecture reference, while preserving accessible controls, honest product states, and current security boundaries.
requiredContent: Shared application shell: Lokr mark, labelled sidebar navigation for Dashboard, CV Manager, Jobs, Applications, Interview Prep, and Settings, with responsive mobile navigation.
Dashboard: summary counts for saved jobs, applications, interviews, and offers; application pipeline; upcoming interviews; continuation tasks; recent applications; activity; and workspace readiness.
CV Manager: CV upload area, document list with name, updated date, type, and actions, plus review-state visibility.
CV Detail, Editor, and Preview: editable CV fields, structured sections, preview pane, save action, version context, and review-safe sample content.
Jobs list and saved jobs: search, saved-jobs view, role, location, and type filters, job rows, and explicit saved state.
Job Detail: job title, company metadata, saved state, overview, requirements, and separate editable notes.
AI CV Match Analysis: explicit analysis action, heuristic match estimate only, source CV and job context, strengths and gaps, provider and data-sharing disclosure before any analysis.
Tailored CV Workspace: original and tailored CV comparison, editable draft context, provenance and review status, with export actions only when a real export capability exists.
Applications Tracker: stage-based board for Saved, Applied, Interview, Offer, and Rejected applications, accessible status changes, application creation, and stable card identities.
Application Detail: overview, status control, timeline, notes, reminders, and application history derived from local actions.
Interview Prep Setup: job and CV selection, manually chosen focus areas, and explicit start-practice action.
Interview Practice: question, guidance, manual answer field, optional recording or feedback controls only when supported, and no fabricated AI feedback.
Settings: honest AI connection status, privacy explanation, and future configuration space without fake provider credentials, test connections, or unsafe local-runner controls.
constraints: Extend the existing Next.js application. Do not replace its framework, shell, local fonts, or existing interaction model.
All visible application terms and user-facing copy must be English.
Preserve the existing Achromatic ledger and open-plane visual system: neutral chrome, flat white surfaces, near-black primary action, and blue #1d5fbf reserved for primary data.
Do not add marketing sections, fabricated users, employers, outcomes, testimonials, hiring predictions, or real-world affiliations.
Keep representative content visibly identified as sample data until replaced with real user data.
AI matching remains a heuristic estimate, never an ATS score or hiring prediction.
Do not send CV or job content to an AI provider without explicit user action, named provider, and clear disclosure of data leaving the machine.
Do not create fake API-key, provider-test, CLI-runner, server-sync, export, or persistence behavior when no supporting backend exists.
Maintain loading, empty, zero, error, and success states; keyboard access; visible focus; responsive desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts; and reduced-motion behavior.
ADR-003 and ADR-004 remain undecided and must not be silently resolved by the UI.
brandInputs: Existing apps/web/src/styles/kit.css: Achromatic ledger tokens, Geist and Geist Mono local font loading, neutral off-white ground, white cards, near-black controls, and blue #1d5fbf data accent.
Existing apps/web/src/components/workspace.tsx: Lokr CSS mark, labelled sidebar shell, hash routes, English navigation labels, and current dashboard-level local interactions.
Supplied twelve-screen wireframe: desktop information architecture and composition reference for Dashboard, CV management, jobs, applications, interview preparation, and settings.
assumptions: The wireframe’s names, companies, dates, counts, and scores are illustrative concept content. They will be replaced by the existing clearly labelled sample dataset until real user data is available.

Continuing implementation means expanding the current dashboard into twelve connected operational views, not claiming that backend storage, AI analysis, exports, audio recording, or external provider integrations already work.
The existing dashboard priority remains adding or saving a job before managing its linked application.
Status changes, filters, tabs, board movements, drawers, and dialogs receive functional transitions only. The interface has no decorative page entrances.
Wireframe controls for API keys, provider testing, and local CLI runners are replaced with truthful unavailable or status-only states until secure backend support is implemented.
Visible English copy applies to all current and new views, including statuses, form labels, errors, empty states, and navigation.
unresolved: A secure, real AI provider configuration and analysis workflow requires backend implementation and explicit user invocation.
No real CVs, jobs, applications, reminders, or interview material have been supplied, so the interface must continue using illustrative sample data.
ADR-004 still governs the final tailored-CV editing workflow and should remain reversible in the UI.
